To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the cloud environment poses unique challenges for data management, (ii) these challenges can be addressed by leveraging the cloud characteristics, (iii) a cloud-bound DBM must be designed to support both the traditional enterprise application workloads as we as new application workloads that exploit the cloud infrastructure, and (iv) a cloud-bound database management system should be designed with a clear vision of the cloud computing evolution.

the cloud is a natural environment for large scale data management systems and that the design of a cloud-bound DBSMS should focus on providing a high level of scalability, availability, and elasticity, and that it should be designed to support a wide range of application demands.

(i) the design space for large scale data management systems in the cloud is very rich, (ii) the design space is not orthogonal, and (iii) there is a trade-off between the ease of programming and performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding and addressing the challenges in developing large scale data management solutions for cloud computing.
the design and analysis of large scale data management systems that are scalable, reliable, and cost effective, and are capable of handling both update heavy applications and ad-hoc analytics.

the following aspects of cloud computing: (i) the challenges posed by cloud computing to the design of database systems, (ii) the design and implementation of scalable database management systems that can support large scale applications, and (iii) the design of novel algorithms and data structures that can be used by such database systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no off-the-shelf solutions for large scale database systems in cloud environment and that there are many open research problems that need to be tackled in this space.
there is no single solution that can be applied to all application domains, and the best solution depends on the application domain and the data management requirements.
the current state-of-the-art is not sufficient to support the needs of the next generation cloud applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current DBMS systems are still far from being ready for the cloud environment.
the current generation of DBMSs have been designed for traditional enterprise applications, and are ill-suited for cloud applications.

the design of large scale database management system for update intensive applications must be driven by the following three factors: (a) the application workload, (b) the underlying hardware and software, and (c) the application deployment model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state of the art is not yet sufficient for the needs of the future.
the current state of the art does not address all the requirements of cloud bound database applications.

the design choices made in the context of the traditional enterprise setting are not necessarily optimal for the cloud setting and that the design of cloud-bound database systems needs to be revisited to address the challenges posed by the cloud environment.
